reviews.comment: CHEM415 with Dr. Russell was my easiest and favorite class that semester, after wine tasting. Pay attention in lectures a little bit, and if you try to answer his questions you'll definitely get easier grading on the exams.  On exams, Try to explain techniques with few words and use lots of pictures. Even better if you make your own pictures.

David Russell was definitely an incredibly intelligent and great researcher... 30 years ago. This guy doesn't post a single grade until the class is over, the lectures are just him asking questions to vague slides, and his class is just dated. Nice enough guy, but the format genuinely sucks. Take home essay style exams and like I said, NO GRADES.

Dr. Russell is extremely knowledgeable on what he's teaching, but expects you to think like a chemist (or perhaps a graduate student). Class isn't mandatory, but if you don't show up to lecture you'll probably be very lost, and as much as he encourages finding online resources they may not be sufficient if you aren't going to class.

I got 9/10 and 10/10 for all the assignments/midterms, but he gave me a B in the course. Dr. Russell doesn't use canvas or keep track of assignments anywhere, and I'm at a complete loss as to how he determined the final letter grade. If I knew I was getting a B I would have asked him about it, but I really thought I had an A. I don't know anymore.

Dr. Russell clearly had a solid understanding of the fundamentals or analytical chemistry. He had the ability to explain concepts very clearly. However, his lectures were not that helpful. It was mainly centered on him asking questions after a brief slide deck. Out of the 5 assignments he gave, only 4 were graded. His grading was also a mystery.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things
